summary.text: 早 means “morning” and “early.” One account reads 日 above 甲 as the sun’s first appearance. A separate analysis proposes that later-bronze forms combine 日 with 棗 as a sound element; the sound comparison does not identify 棗 in any particular inscription.

formation.text: The character has competing proposed analyses. In one, 日 depicts the sun and 甲 contributes “first,” suggesting the sun’s initial appearance. Another analysis of later-bronze forms treats 日 as a meaning element and 棗 as a sound element, sometimes reduced to 朿. 棗 and 早 have related but nonidentical Old Chinese reconstructions in the same system. This sound comparison is compatible with the proposal but does not establish 棗’s identity in a particular inscription, or a sequence linking the two analyses.

components.text: In the 日+甲 account, 日 depicts the sun. In the later-bronze account, it contributes meaning to a phonosemantic construction; these are distinct analyses.
In the 日+甲 interpretation, 甲 is understood as “first,” completing the proposed idea of the sun’s initial appearance. This role belongs to that account, not to every reported form.

A later-bronze analysis identifies 棗 as the sound element, sometimes reduced to 朿. The regular form’s lower 十 is separately explained as developed from seal-script 甲; it should not be treated as a visible 棗.

sound_limitation.text: The Old Chinese comparison supports a sound resemblance, but does not by itself establish 棗’s identity as the sound element in a particular inscription.

sound.text: The Old Chinese reconstructions share related segmental material but are not identical; this comparison is compatible with the proposed sound role, not proof of it.
Both are reconstructed with the same Middle Chinese reading in this system.
Both have the modern Mandarin reading zǎo; this present-day match does not prove an ancient sound role.

history.text: The regular form’s lower 十 is explained as a transformation of seal-script 甲. A separate later-bronze analysis identifies 棗, sometimes reduced to 朿, as a sound element. The evidence does not establish a single graphic sequence linking these accounts.

Graph structure is separate from spelling practice. 棗 (jujube) and 蚤 (flea) are reported as signs reused to write the different word 早 because of proposed sound resemblance, rather than because their meanings developed into “early.” Their readings provide comparisons, but the evidence does not establish why or when either borrowing occurred. Another account proposes oracle-bone 草 for the word 早 and reports Qin and Han uses of 早 and 皁 for a word related to 皂.

uncertainties.text: The accounts differ on whether early forms of 早 already wrote the word meaning “early.” The proposed oracle-bone and Qin/Han spelling history remains unresolved; detailed artifact contexts are not available here.

An early pictograph for an acorn related to 皂 is proposed elsewhere, but the supplied evidence does not establish that an ancient 早-shaped graph depicted an acorn or that the depicted object had the sound of the word “early.”

senses.period: Later bronze inscription; exact date unresolved
senses.text: A later-bronze inscription is cited for 早 used with the sense “early” or “sooner.” This records a use of the graph, not the earliest attestation of the spoken word.
The Shuowen account glosses 早 as “morning,” and the character remains used with this meaning. This evidence does not identify it as the earliest attested use of the spoken word.
“Already” appears in a dictionary sense inventory, but no dated example here establishes when this use arose.

developments.text: Both meanings are recorded, but the evidence does not show whether “early/sooner” developed from “morning.”

limitations.text: Dictionary sense lists do not establish chronological order. No supported path is given from “morning” to “already” or “initial.”

棗 and 蚤 are reported as signs reused to write the different word 早, rather than as meanings that developed from “jujube” or “flea.” This is proposed graph borrowing on sound resemblance; the cited readings provide comparisons but do not establish why or when either borrowing occurred.

overview.text: 早 means “morning” and “early.” One account reads 日 above 甲 as the sun’s first appearance. Another proposes that a later-bronze 日+棗 sign was reused for “morning/early” because the words sounded alike; the sound match and 棗 identification are not confirmed for a particular inscription.

components.text: 日 depicts the sun in one account and contributes meaning in another.
In one account, 甲 means “first,” suggesting the sun’s initial appearance.
棗 is proposed as a sound element in a later-bronze analysis; its identity in a particular inscription is uncertain.

relationships.text: In the 日+甲 analysis, 日 depicts the sun in a proposed scene of its initial appearance.
The alternative later-bronze analysis assigns 日 a meaning contribution in a phonosemantic construction.
In the 日+甲 interpretation, 甲 contributes “first” to the proposed idea of the sun’s initial appearance.

A later-bronze analysis identifies 棗 as a sound element, sometimes reduced to 朿. In Baxter–Sagart, the Old Chinese reconstructions are related but not identical (棗 *[ts]ˤuʔ; 早 *Nə.tsˤuʔ), while both have Middle Chinese tsawX in that system and modern Mandarin zǎo. These comparisons fit the proposed analysis but do not establish 棗’s identity in a particular inscription.
